text:
sara: Heads up — provisioning in us-west2 popped at ~09:07 UTC, GPU launch median latency up to ~120s and ~18% launch failures. Noticed a bunch of nodes marked busy due to local disk I/O.

infra-bot: [ALERT] us-west2-gpu-provisioning latency spike (trigger=queue_depth). Affected ASG: gpu-pool-6. 120 failures in last 5m.

matt: grabbing iostat and dmesg now. early look: huge iowait bursts on nvme followed by dozens of kworker/blockmap_compact entries in kern.log. snippet:```
May 15 09:06:42 gnode-123 kernel: kworker/3:2: blockmap_compact: started
May 15 09:06:42 gnode-123 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O 0x... error - curr q depth 255
May 15 09:06:44 gnode-123 kernel: kworker/3:2: blockmap_compact: finished duration=1843ms
```

nidhi: that aligns with the overlay snapshot retention tweak we pushed last week (reduce snapshot ttl to 7d, and a compact job runs to shrink blockmaps). thought it would reduce long-term metadata, not cause spikes.

reza: I think the compact job cron ended up set to run on the hour across the fleet due to a templating bug — so everyone runs at the same time (no jitter). during that window, background compaction saturates the NVMe controller. we should never compact during provisioning windows.

jen: short-term mitigation? can we stop compaction on nodes currently serving provisioning requests and drain outstanding compactions? :eyes:

matt: temporary actions we can execute now: 1) disable the compaction timer on affected hosts, 2) throttle compaction with ionice or systemd IOWeight, 3) add a quick probe to pause compaction if /proc/interrupts or iostat shows qdepth>200. example commands (run via fleet-run):```bash
sudo systemctl stop blockmap-compact.timer
sudo systemctl stop blockmap-compact.service || pkill -f blockmap_compact
# set low IO priority for compaction process (if it respawns): sudo ionice -c2 -n7 -p $(pgrep -f blockmap_compact)
# quick iostat check: iostat -x 1 3 /dev/nvme0n1
```

nidhi: rolling the retention revert out now to avoid re-triggering. I'll also add jitter to the template so compacts land within a 6hr spread.

reza: long-term we should: 1) make compaction fleet-aware (skip when provisioning pressure > X), 2) rate-limit per-host compaction IO, 3) move heavy compactions to a maintenance window with controlled concurrency, 4) add a probe in the provisioner that rejects starts if local IOPS > threshold instead of letting provisioning pile up.

jen: agree. matt — can you PR an auto-throttle (detect qdepth or provisioning holes) and a per-host disable flag this afternoon? reza — please patch the cron template to add randomized jitter and a 6hr spread. nidhi — please hold the retention change until we validate. I'll send an incident note and set the postmortem owners.

matt: on it. I'll also add a temporary alert: if blockmap_compact runs >1s and iowait >50% for >30s, mute compaction and notify. putting patch in staging now.

sara: thanks team — freeing this thread but keep updates here. ping me if any host still failing after the stop commands. :thumbsup:
